correctness.rationale: For each real strictly positive homogeneous quartic Q in every integer dimension d>=2, the Fourier transform of Gaussian times Q-Delta Q/(8pi) equals itself by exact Gaussian differentiation. Its polar negative-set radius squared is h=(d+2)/(2pi)+Delta_S A/(8pi A). Since A>0 on the sphere, the negative set is bounded and has exact volume omega_d E[h_+^(d/2)]. Integration by parts gives E[Delta_S A/A]=E[|grad_S log A|^2], and Jensen for d/2>=1 gives the claimed lower bound. Fisher information vanishes iff A constant, giving the sharp unique radial equality class. All constants and the d=2 planar excess formula are derived directly. Supplementary checker.py successfully ran 173 exact symbolic and numerical assertions. The finite checks are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 definite-set uncertainty problem calls for sharp lower bounds on sign-defined sets of Fourier eigenfunctions; the theorem settles the first nontrivial Fourier +1 Hermite band, across all dimensions, with exact optimizer classification and a quantitative angular Fisher-information stability factor. It is not a single arbitrary quartic or a numerical constant, but an all-dimension classification of a canonical finite oscillator-energy slice. It does not claim global optimality beyond the band.
